title: Gimbel–Thomassen Problem 3
statement_text: Is there a polynomial-time algorithm to test the 3-colorability of triangle-free graphs embeddable in a fixed surface?
context_text: For non-planar surfaces, Grötzsch's theorem does not directly generalise and no uniform characterisation of 3-colorability (analogous to Theorem 1.3 for the projective plane) is known. Gimbel and Thomassen raised this algorithmic question as Problem 3 in their paper on quadrangulations and 3-colorability.
paper_contribution: This paper develops the foundational technical theory — specifically a linear bound $|V(H)| \leq 1715|V(C)|$ on the size of 4-critical subgraphs in a disk (Theorem 1.6) — that is used in the subsequent papers of this series to resolve this question in the affirmative.
notes: Bibliography entry [7] is not reproduced in the extracted text, so the year of the original problem cannot be confirmed.
paper_title: Three-coloring triangle-free graphs on surfaces II. 4-critical graphs in a disk

title: Conjecture 1.7
statement_text: For every integer $k \geq 5$, there exists an integer $K$ with the following property. Let $G$ be a planar graph of girth at least five, let $C_1, C_2$ be two cycles in $G$ of lengths at most $k$, and for every $v \in V(G)$ let $L(v)$ be a set such that $|L(v)| = 1$ if $v \in V(C_1 \cup C_2)$ and $|L(v)| \geq 3$ otherwise. If there exists no proper coloring $\phi$ of $G$ such that $\phi(v) \in L(v)$ for every $v \in V(G)$, then $G$ has a subgraph $H$ on at most $K$ vertices such that $C_1$ and $C_2$ are subgraphs of $H$ and there exists no proper coloring $\psi$ of $H$ such that $\psi(v) \in L(v)$ for every $v \in V(H)$.
context_text: Here a proper coloring $\phi$ with $\phi(v)\in L(v)$ for all $v$ is a list coloring from the lists $L$; vertices of the two cycles $C_1,C_2$ have a single allowed colour, i.e. they are precolored, and the conjecture asks that whenever this precoloring of two short cycles does not extend to an $L$-coloring of $G$, there is a bounded-size obstruction containing both cycles. The paper is part of a series on 3-colorability of graphs on surfaces with restricted triangles; its main result is the single-cycle, non-list version: if $G$ is a planar graph of girth at least five, $C$ a cycle of $G$ and $\phi$ a 3-coloring of $C$ that does not extend to a 3-coloring of $G$, then some subgraph $H$ of $G$ containing $C$ with $|V(H)|\le 1715|V(C)|$ already has no 3-coloring extending $\phi$ (Dvořák and Kawarabayashi generalized this to list coloring with a better constant). The authors' broader result states that there is an absolute constant $K$ such that every 4-critical graph (not 3-colorable but every proper subgraph is) drawn in a surface of Euler genus $\gamma$ with no separating cycles of length at most four and with $t$ triangles satisfies $\sum|f|\le K(t+\gamma)$, the sum being over faces of length at least five. They ask whether the analogue of this bound for graphs of girth at least five holds in the list-coloring setting, and note that an affirmative answer would follow from the conjecture. Luke Postle (private communication) believes he has a proof, not yet written down at the time of the paper. In the paper's displayed conjecture the final condition reads $\phi(v)\in L(v)$, an evident typo for $\psi(v)\in L(v)$.
notes: The PDF extraction renders the final clause with $\phi$ instead of $\psi$; from context the intended quantifier variable in the conclusion is $\psi$, corrected here.
